comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation is subject to an FDIC special assessment to recover losses from the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, with quarterly collections beginning in Q2 2024; the accrual was $1.7 billion as of December 31, 2024, compared to $2.1 billion in 2023, and the liability amount may change based on the FDIC's updated loss estimates.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose expenses and accruals related to the FDIC special assessment to recover losses from Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank. Citi recorded $203 million in expense for 2024, with a prior year expense of $1,706 million. Bank of America reports a significantly larger accrual liability of $1.7 billion as of December 31, 2024 (compared to $2.1 billion in 2023), reflecting its estimated share of the assessment. While Citi discloses the annual expense flow, Bank of America highlights the cumulative accrual balance and notes that quarterly collections began in Q2 2024.

sentences.text: Citi recorded $203 million and $1,706 million in Other operating expenses for the years ended 2024 and 2023, respectively, related to the FDIC's final rule implementing a special assessment to recover the uninsured deposit losses from the failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.

In 2023, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) issued a final rule to impose a special assessment to recover certain estimated losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) arising from the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.
As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Corporation's accrual for its estimated share of the FDIC special assessment was $1.7 billion and $2.1 billion.
